title: Fusion in the energy system
description: World energy demand, the fuel and the waste of fusion compared with fission, and a sorting task that separates established results from institutional plans and corporate claims.

sources.title: Ember: Global Electricity Review 2026, 2025 in review
sources.note: 2025: demand +2.8 % (+849 TWh); renewables 33.8 % (10 730 TWh), coal 33.0 % (10 476 TWh), gas 21.8 %, wind and solar together 17.3 %.

sources.title: Ember: World electricity data (shares in 2025)
sources.note: Nuclear 8.9 %, hydro 14 %, wind 8.5 %, solar 8.7 %, low-carbon sources 43 %. The 5.1 % 'other' row of the unit's table is the remainder (bioenergy, oil and other sources), computed from these shares.

sources.title: World energy supply and consumption (Wikipedia): primary energy by fuel, 2024 (Energy Institute 2025)
sources.note: Coal, oil and gas: more than four fifths of primary energy in 2024 (about 82 % by the substitution method, about 87 % by energy content); the fuels listed sum to about 590 EJ.

sources.title: IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 °C (Wikipedia summary)
sources.note: Net CO₂ emissions about 45 % below 2010 levels by 2030 and net zero around 2050 for 1.5 °C (published 8 October 2018).

sources.title: Tritium (Wikipedia): half-life 12.32 years, breeding from lithium-6 (+4.8 MeV) and lithium-7
Kleinman Center for Energy Policy, University of Pennsylvania: Tritium — a few kilograms can make or break nuclear fusion (6 March 2025)
sources.note: Civilian tritium inventory about 25 kg (2024); Canadian CANDU reactors about 2 kg per year; a 1 GW fusion plant needs nearly 55 kg per year; stored tritium shrinks by about 5 % per year.

sources.title: ITER Organization: Tritium breeding (last modified 2026-10-06)
sources.note: Lithium in the blanket absorbs a neutron and gives tritium and helium; ITER will test tritium breeding in test blanket modules; a power plant must breed all its own tritium.

sources.title: ITER Organization: Advantages of fusion
sources.note: No high-activity, long-lived waste; materials recyclable within 100 years; no Fukushima-type accident possible; lithium reserves for more than 1000 years on land.

sources.title: ITER Organization: Safety and environment
sources.note: A few grams of tritium in the plasma at any time; fast neutrons activate material surfaces; waste of very low, low or medium activity; most of its radioisotopes have half-lives under ten years.

sources.title: Fusion power (Wikipedia): waste, safety, fuel resources, costs
sources.note: No runaway reaction (seconds of fuel in the machine); waste mostly low-level, some intermediate-level; projected costs of future plants are estimates.

sources.title: Deuterium (Wikipedia): 155.76 deuterium atoms per million hydrogen atoms in ocean water (about 1 in 6420)
EUROfusion: JET's final tritium experiments yield new fusion energy record (8 February 2024)
sources.note: 69.26 MJ of heat in one pulse of about six seconds from 0.21 mg of fuel, in the campaign of autumn 2023.

sources.title: National Ignition Facility (Wikipedia): ignition on 5 December 2022
sources.note: 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser light; the laser pulse took about 300 MJ of electricity to produce.

sources.title: WEST (formerly Tore Supra) (Wikipedia): 1337 s plasma on 12 February 2025
ITER (Wikipedia): 2024 baseline, costs, no electricity
sources.note: Construction estimated at EUR 5.9 billion over ten years (2006); later estimates of construction and operation EUR 18–22 billion. Research operation 2034, deuterium–deuterium 2035, deuterium–tritium 2039 (July 2024 baseline); 500 MW of fusion heat from 50 MW of heating (Q = 10); ITER will not produce electricity.

sources.title: GOV.UK: £2.5 billion for world-first prototype fusion energy plant (12 June 2025)
sources.note: STEP at the former West Burton A power station, targeting first operations in 2040.

sources.title: Helion Energy (Wikipedia): agreement to supply Microsoft from a 50 MW plant by 2028
SPARC (tokamak) (Wikipedia): first plasma planned for 2027, Q > 1 shortly after, expected Q ≈ 11
World Nuclear News: Fusion industry raised USD 4.5 billion in past year, report says (14 July 2026)
sources.note: Fusion Industry Association survey 2026: 56 companies; USD 4.48 billion in the year to July 2026, USD 14.24 billion in total; 71 % of the companies expect power on the grid 'by the 2030s'.
